subject: Mutual Action Plan — Provisioning Sprint & Cutover Milestone (API token handoff, IP safelist, peering windows)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Victor Chan <victor.chan@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan — Provisioning Sprint & Cutover Milestone (API token handoff, IP safelist, peering windows)

Hi Victor —

Thanks again for the productive kickoff yesterday. I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) that captures the provisioning sprint we discussed and the proposed cutover milestone. The MAP focuses on the four items you flagged as blockers for a production-like evaluation environment:

- API token handoff (ephemeral token vs. managed API key)
- Organization & tenant setup (test tenants, role mappings)
- IP safelist / firewall rules (CIDR ranges we need whitelisted)
- VPC peering windows and maintenance blackout periods

Proposed near-term cadence:
1) Today (Oct 15): confirm owners and access list
2) Tue Oct 19: API keys issued to your eng sandbox & brief key-rotation guidance
3) Wed Oct 20: IP allowlist applied and initial smoke tests
4) Thu Oct 21: VPC peering scheduled during 02:00–05:00 PT (low traffic) — rollback plan included

Please review the attached MAP_Draft_Veridian_v1.docx and let me know any changes to owners or the dates above. If the dates work, I’ll loop in our networking SME (Jonas) to provide the peering snippet and final firewall ranges.

Quick asks: could you confirm the sandbox owner and the contact for procurement (for the SOW) so we can align on timing?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: MAP_Draft_Veridian_v1.docx (docx, 98KB)
From: Victor Chan <victor.chan@veridianhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@veridianhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan — Provisioning Sprint & Cutover Milestone (API token handoff, IP safelist, peering windows)

Marissa —

Thanks for sending this over. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) IP allowlist: can you provide the exact CIDR ranges you need whitelisted? Our security team requires a /28 granularity for peering endpoints.
2) Peering window: the Thu 02:00–05:00 PT window looks fine but we need to avoid Thursdays where we run overnight batch jobs. Can you propose a fallback on Fri 03:00–06:00 PT?
3) API token handoff: we prefer time-bound ephemeral tokens where possible. If Redwood requires a static API key for the initial smoke tests, we’ll accept it but will need an automatic rotation after 48 hours.

Sandbox owner: myself (Victor Chan) for initial testing; I’ll provide an eng contact for deeper networking tasks (adding: priya.singh@veridianhealth.com). Procurement: procurement@veridianhealth.com — they’ll need the SOW and an estimated monthly commit number for budget.

Appreciate the quick turnaround; could your team reply with the CIDR ranges and the fallback peering window?

Best,
Victor
Victor Chan
Principal Engineer, Veridian Health
victor.chan@veridianhealth.com

Victor —

Thanks — good questions. Quick responses inline: 

1) IP allowlist: primary peering endpoint IPs we need whitelisted are: 34.82.120.16/28 and 35.201.64.32/28. For management plane (console/API): 3.17.128.0/26. These are the ranges our peering infra will use; Jonas can provide a fuller list if you need /32s.

2) Peering fallback: Fri 03:00–06:00 PT works for us as a secondary window. We’ll mark Thu as primary and Fri as fallback in the MAP.

3) API tokens: we support issuing time-bound ephemeral tokens for the evaluation. For the initial smoke test we can provide a short-lived static API key valid for 24 hours and coordinate immediate rotation after verification — we’ll include rotation automation instructions in the runbook.

I attached a short Provisioning_Runbook.xlsx with step-by-step actions, owner assignments, and the rollback checklist. Link to the HubSpot deal is below so procurement can attach the SOW to the record: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789

If this all looks good I’ll:
- finalize the MAP and update owners (today)
- schedule the peering maintenance in PagerDuty for the primary window (Thu 02:00–05:00 PT) with a Fri fallback
- have Jonas drop the final peering snippet and BGP ASN notes before Tuesday’s key issuance

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: RE: Mutual Action Plan — Provisioning Sprint & Cutover Milestone (API token handoff, IP safelist, peering windows)

Victor / team —

Dropping the technical notes and a minimal peering snippet below. Two implementation notes up front:

- We strongly recommend ephemeral tokens for the MAP; however we can provide a one-time static API key for the 24-hour smoke test and then rotate to ephemeral tokens programmatically (scripts included).
- For VPC peering we’ll use shared routes; BGP is not required for the initial eval. If you require BGP, we’ll need ASN exchange (our ASN: 64512).

Firewall / allowlist (minimum to run endpoints):
- Inference endpoints: 34.82.120.16/28, 35.201.64.32/28
- Control / API plane: 3.17.128.0/26
- Peering health checks (TCP/443): 34.82.120.24 and 35.201.64.40 (please allow /32 for health checks)

Peering config snippet (stub attached):
- Local VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (Veridian Sandbox)
- Remote VPC: rwd-inference-prod-peer (Redwood evaluation peer)
- Routes to advertise: 10.10.0.0/16 (your tenant namespaces)
- ASN: 64512 (Redwood)

Rollback plan (short):
1) Disable routes advertised from Redwood;
2) Remove allowlist entries we added;
3) Revert DNS entries to previous endpoints (TTL 60s will help).

Attachment: peering_config_snippet.txt (text, 3KB)

Please confirm acceptance of the CIDRs and the Fri fallback by Monday Oct 18 EOD so we can lock the SOW dates with procurement.

—Jonas
Staff Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
